A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of LLM reasoning under output-length constraints. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 28 LLMs on GSM8K and MATH500, including stopping-method and prompt comparisons, model-size analyses, and measured latency profiles.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results, expands the evaluated model set to 30, and reports additional experiments on MMLU STEM and ACPBench in Section 6.

M1.justification: Both versions use direct termination and early stopping with the same 25-token allowance, concluding message, and three prompt styles. v3 Section 3.2 clarifies continuation, answer extraction, and handling of naturally completed responses; this documents the existing procedure rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematical reasoning on GSM8K and MATH500. v3 Section 6 additionally reports evaluations on mmlu_stem, covering broader STEM subjects, and ACPBench, covering reasoning about actions and plans. These substantially broaden the tested task domains.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and the corresponding appendix comparisons add Qwen-2.5-72B and Llama-3.1-70B to the compared model set. The existing models, stopping-method alternatives, and three prompt comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The model configurations expand to 70B and 72B, and Section 6 adds cross-domain prompt, size, and model-type comparisons, including budgets up to 1000 versus 4096 tokens. The original mathematics splits, zero-shot greedy decoding, reference token budgets, 25-token allowance, and A800 latency setup remain unchanged. The additional domains receive only brief protocol descriptions.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds quantitative examination of the response-length explanation for smaller models outperforming larger ones. Section 6 also checks whether the prompt, size, and model-type findings generalize beyond mathematics. The existing prompt comparisons and size and latency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars for its experiments. The newly reported output-length means and medians are descriptive results, without a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All shared entries in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. New Table 1 scores are 95.8/83.2 for Qwen-2.5-72B and 94.9/62.6 for Llama-3.1-70B on GSM8K/MATH500. v3 also reports 14.6%/14.2% shorter median/mean outputs for Qwen 7B versus 14B and qualitative cross-domain findings. Its Figure 4 places four DRD-Qwen-7B curves at budgets 25 tokens higher than v1 Figure 5, with unchanged accuracy values.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs. v3's Budget minus alpha notation, with alpha equal to 25, restates the existing stopping allowance rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning or a substantive formal definition.

C1.justification: The empirical-study contribution and five central findings retain their meaning: early stopping helps, prompt choice matters, larger and reasoning-specialized models are not universally superior, and medium-sized models can be latency-optimal. The additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6 cautiously interprets generalization beyond mathematics and notes that prompt-style benefits are limited on ACPBench. Section 5.5 makes deployment guidance more specific to models around 7B. The formal Limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies which output segment is scored, when concluding-message injection is unnecessary, and how numerical and symbolic answer equality is checked. New Figure 9 illustrates input construction, and an examples-website link is added. Existing chat templates, software versions, and the promise of future code/data release are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on following length constraints, MMLU, and ACPBench, and explicitly explains its exclusion of prompt-only length control. It removes the latent-space reasoning, LIMO, and s1 discussions and citations. The overall positioning as an empirical evaluation remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method, setup, and findings undergo extensive prose revision. The appendices are reorganized into separate method, experimental-setup, and evaluation sections, and a Discussion section is inserted. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and relocated, prompt material is moved and reformatted, and v3 Figure 9 adds an input-construction illustration. Tables and appendix grids accommodate the two additional models, while legends and budget ticks are revised. The overall layout and most existing plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 explains budget enforcement and scoring more clearly, strengthens the response-length interpretation, and adds larger-model checks and initial evidence beyond mathematics. These are useful but limited gains: the core results remain stable, and the new MMLU STEM and ACPBench findings lack numerical score tables and detailed protocols.
